books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.blurb: Nietzsche's prophet descends from the mountain with the Übermensch, the will to power, and the eternal recurrence — a poetic manifesto for creating your own values.
books.title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra

books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.blurb: Faith, doubt, guilt, and redemption collide in the Karamazov family — Dostoevsky's final and greatest novel on the struggle between good and evil in the human soul.
books.title: The Brothers Karamazov

books.author: Bertrand Russell
books.blurb: Russell diagnoses the modern causes of unhappiness — competition, boredom, fatigue, envy — and prescribes zest, affection, and impersonal interests as the way out.
books.title: The Conquest of Happiness

books.author: Plato
books.blurb: Socrates asks what justice is and builds an ideal city to find the answer — the founding text of Western political philosophy, with the allegory of the cave at its heart.
books.title: The Republic

books.author: Paulo Coelho
books.blurb: Santiago the shepherd follows his Personal Legend across the desert — a fable about listening to your heart, reading the omens, and the treasure you find by seeking it.
books.title: The Alchemist

books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.blurb: Nietzsche dismantles the prejudices of philosophers and sketches the 'free spirit' — master vs. slave morality, the will to power, and philosophy with a hammer.
books.title: Beyond Good and Evil

books.author: Daniel Kahneman
books.blurb: Kahneman maps the mind's two gears — fast intuition and slow reasoning — and the biases (anchoring, framing, loss aversion) that quietly steer everyday judgment.
books.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
Crime and Punishment
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.blurb: # Crime and Punishment ### A 20-Minute Read **Fyodor Dostoevsky (1866) — Episode 8 of the Top 10 Books series** *A former student with a theory, an axe, and a fever.

books.title: Sapiens
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.blurb: Sapiens asks how Homo sapiens, once a marginal ape among several human species, came to build cities, money, empires, and rockets — by believing shared stories and cooperating at scale.

books.title: The Art of War
books.author: Sun Tzu
books.blurb: The Art of War is a manual for armed conflict written in China roughly two thousand five hundred years ago — and it is mostly famous for arguing that the best war is the one you never fight.

books.title: Tao Te Ching
books.author: Lao-Tzu
books.blurb: One of the shortest great books ever written — roughly five thousand words in eighty-one chapters — the Tao Te Ching argues that the Way cannot be named, that water overcomes rock, and that the best leadership looks like doing nothing at all.

books.title: The Forty Rules of Love
books.author: Elif Shafak
books.blurb: Elif Shafak's million-copy bestseller braids two love stories eight centuries apart: a bored Massachusetts housewife reading her way toward a new life, and the thirteenth-century friendship between the mystic poet Rumi and the wandering dervish Shams of Tabriz. Between them run forty rules of love — a spiritual operating system for dismantling the ego, one small death at a time.

books.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
books.author: Amor Towles
books.blurb: Amor Towles's 2016 novel traps Count Alexander Rostov — a Russian aristocrat sentenced in 1922 to lifelong house arrest inside Moscow's Metropol Hotel — and asks what remains when everything that defined a person is taken away. Across three decades of purges and war, the Count learns that freedom is not the absence of constraint but what you choose to do with it.

books.title: The Three-Body Problem
books.author: Liu Cixin
books.blurb: Liu Cixin's Hugo-winning first-contact epic opens in China's Cultural Revolution, where a young astrophysicist's despair leads her to invite an alien civilization to Earth — and follows the fallout forty years later, when a physicist starts seeing a countdown only he can see. Hard science, deep grief, and the most vertigo-inducing ideas in modern science fiction.

books.title: The Dark Forest
books.author: Liu Cixin
books.blurb: The second book of Liu Cixin's Remembrance of Earth's Past trilogy: the dark forest theory, the Wallfacers, the droplet that annihilates humanity's fleet, and Luo Ji's fifty-four years holding the fate of two civilizations.

books.title: Death's End
books.author: Liu Cixin
books.blurb: The trilogy's cosmic finale: a brain fired into space, fairy tales hiding the secrets of the universe, the dual-vector foil that flattens the solar system, and a fish tank drifting at the end of everything.

books.title: High Output Management
books.author: Andy Grove
books.blurb: Andy Grove — Hungarian refugee, Berkeley PhD, co-founder and later CEO of Intel — wrote the most durable management manual of the modern era while running one of the most important companies on earth. His thesis: management is a production process.

books.title: Zero to One
books.author: Peter Thiel
books.blurb: Every moment in business happens only once. The next Bill Gates will not build an operating system; the next Larry Page will not build a search engine.

books.title: 10% Happier
books.author: Dan Harris
books.blurb: Dan Harris was a rising star at ABC News — a war correspondent turned anchor — when, in 2004, he had a full-blown panic attack live on *Good Morning America*, in front of millions of viewers.

books.title: The Power of Now
books.author: Eckhart Tolle
books.blurb: The Power of Now is Eckhart Tolle's 1997 guide to a single, deceptively simple insight: you are not your mind. The book argues that almost all human suffering comes from identification with the compulsive, involuntary stream of thinking, and that peace becomes available the moment you disidentify from it and rest attention in the present moment — the Now, the only place life actually happens.

books.title: Nexus
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.blurb: Nexus is Yuval Noah Harari's history of how human beings learned to connect through information, and why that connection has never guaranteed wisdom.

books.title: The Anarchy
books.author: William Dalrymple
books.blurb: In 1599, a group of London merchants formed a joint-stock company to trade in spices; within a hundred and sixty years, that company had conquered much of India, collected the taxes of Bengal, and commanded an army larger than that of many European states.

books.author: George Orwell
books.blurb: Winston Smith is a minor official in Oceania, a totalitarian superstate ruled by the Party and its symbolic leader, Big Brother. Winston's job at the Ministry of Truth is to rewrite old records so the past always agrees with the present.

books.title: The Better Angels of Our Nature
books.author: Steven Pinker
books.blurb: Steven Pinker's *The Better Angels of Our Nature*, published in 2011, makes a large and surprising claim: violence, in almost every measurable form, has declined over the long sweep of human history, and it may be the most important development that has ever happened to our species.

books.title: Paper Girl
books.author: Beth Macy
books.blurb: Beth Macy grew up poor in Urbana, Ohio, a town of about eleven thousand people, in the nineteen seventies and nineteen eighties. Her father was a housepainter and an alcoholic, known as the town drunk.

books.title: The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny
books.author: Kiran Desai
books.blurb: Sonia and Sunny glimpse each other on an overnight train in India and are instantly attracted — and instantly embarrassed, because their grandparents once tried to arrange a match between them. That embarrassment drives them apart before love can begin.

books.title: Factfulness
books.author: Hans Rosling
books.blurb: Factfulness begins with a quiz that will make you feel foolish, and then explains — kindly, relentlessly — why feeling foolish is the appropriate response. Hans Rosling spent decades asking Nobel laureates, Davos elites, medical students, and ordinary citizens the same simple questions about the world.

books.title: Flashlight
books.author: Susan Choi
books.blurb: One summer evening in 1978, ten-year-old Louisa walks a Japanese breakwater with her father Serk, who carries a flashlight and cannot swim. She is found soaked and barely conscious; he is never found — and four generations of family history turn on that single unexplained night.

books.title: A Marriage at Sea
books.author: Sophie Elmhirst
books.blurb: In June 1972, Maurice and Maralyn Bailey, a British couple from Derby, England, sold almost everything they owned, left their jobs, and set sail from Southampton in their roughly thirty-one-foot yacht, the Auralyn, bound for a new life in New Zealand. Then a wounded sperm whale sank their boat in the Pacific, and they survived 118 days adrift on a tiny raft.

books.title: Business Adventures
books.author: John Brooks
books.blurb: Twelve classic tales from Wall Street and corporate America — a sudden market crash in 1962, Ford's doomed Edsel, the rise of Xerox, an insider trading case, and a grocer who tried to corner his own stock. Warren Buffett lent it to Bill Gates, who called it the best business book he had ever read.

books.author: Andrew Ross Sorkin
books.blurb: Andrew Ross Sorkin, the New York Times DealBook founder and CNBC co-anchor whose Too Big to Fail defined how the 2008 financial crisis is told, spent roughly eight years researching the original catastrophe. 1929 rebuilds the boom and the Great Crash through the people who made them: Charles Mitchell, the salesman-banker whose National City Bank pushed stocks on ordinary savers; Thomas Lamont and the partners of J.P. Morgan, summoned to organize private rescues because no public machinery existed.

books.title: Stone Yard Devotional
books.author: Charlotte Wood
books.blurb: An unnamed, middle-aged woman walks away from her life in Sydney. She is burnt out from years of work at a Threatened Species Rescue Centre, worn down by the daily accounting of loss in the natural world, and her marriage to Alex is failing.

books.title: Range
books.author: David Epstein
books.blurb: Most of us have been told, in one form or another, to pick a lane early and stay in it. Find your thing as a child, practice it for ten thousand hours, specialize ever more narrowly, and success will follow.

books.title: We the People
books.author: Jill Lepore
books.blurb: Jill Lepore, Harvard historian and author of These Truths, tells the history of the United States Constitution from an angle almost no one uses: through the amendments — above all, through the amendments that failed.

books.title: Mother Emanuel
books.author: Kevin Sack
books.blurb: The story of one Charleston church — Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church — told across two centuries, from its roots in a breakaway by free and enslaved Black Methodists in 1818 to the murder of nine worshippers there in 2015, and the forgiveness some of their families offered two days later. Kevin Sack argues that forgiveness at Emanuel was an inherited practice: a religious discipline and a survival tool forged under enslavement, carried alongside an equally long tradition of resistance.

books.title: The Coming Wave
books.author: Mustafa Suleyman
books.blurb: A wave of powerful technologies — above all artificial intelligence and synthetic biology — is building now and will reshape medicine, work, war, and politics within a decade.

books.title: What We Can Know
books.author: Ian McEwan
books.blurb: Ian McEwan's seventeenth novel, published in 2025, is a literary mystery set a century from now about a poem nobody has ever read. In 2119, England is an archipelago after a climate catastrophe and a nuclear accident known as the Derangement.

books.title: The Inner Game of Tennis
books.author: Timothy Gallwey
books.blurb: *The Inner Game of Tennis* argues that the hardest opponent most players ever face is not across the net but inside their own heads.

upcoming.title: There Is No Place for Us
upcoming.author: Brian Goldstone
